examples.en: Australia is in the southern hemisphere, so December is summer.
In the southern hemisphere the seasons are opposite to the north.
You can see the Southern Cross in the southern sky.
If you travel to the southern hemisphere, it's hot even at Christmas.

examples.ko: 칠레는 남반구에 길게 뻗어 있는 나라예요.
examples.en: Chile is a country stretching long in the southern hemisphere.
The southern and northern hemispheres are divided by the equator.

explain: 짝말은 '북반구'이고, 지구를 적도로 나눌 때 써요. 호주나 뉴질랜드처럼 계절이 한국과 반대인 곳을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '북반구', and it is used when dividing the globe at the equator. It often comes up for places like Australia or New Zealand, where the seasons are opposite to Korea's.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 서울의 달동네를 배경으로 해요.
examples.en: That movie is set in a hillside neighborhood in Seoul.
The alleys of the hillside neighborhood are narrow with many steps.

examples.ko: 할머니는 어릴 때 달동네에서 살았다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said she lived in a hillside neighborhood as a child.
The night view from the hillside neighborhood is really beautiful.

examples.ko: 요즘 달동네에 벽화를 그려서 관광지가 됐어요.
examples.en: These days, murals were painted in the hillside neighborhood and it became a tourist spot.

examples.ko: 달동네의 오래된 집들이 하나둘 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: The old houses of the hillside neighborhood are disappearing one by one.

explain: 산비탈이나 높은 곳에 있는 가난한 동네를 말해요. 옛날 이야기, 영화, 드라마에서 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '산동네'가 있고, 지금은 벽화마을처럼 바뀐 곳도 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a poor neighborhood on a hillside or high ground. It often appears in stories about the past, movies and dramas. A similar word is '산동네', and some such places have turned into mural villages today.

examples.ko: 저는 시골에서 자라서 도회지 생활이 처음엔 낯설었어요.
examples.en: I grew up in the countryside, so city life felt strange at first.

examples.ko: 많은 젊은이가 일자리를 찾아 도회지로 떠나요.
examples.en: Many young people leave for the city to find jobs.

examples.ko: 도회지 사람들은 밤늦게까지 불이 켜진 거리를 좋아해요.
examples.en: City people like streets that stay lit late into the night.

examples.ko: 할머니는 도회지에 사는 손주들이 보고 싶다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said she misses her grandchildren who live in the city.

examples.ko: 도회지에서 살다 보니 별을 볼 일이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: Living in the city, I hardly ever get to see stars.

examples.ko: 방학마다 도회지 친척 집에 가서 며칠씩 지내요.
examples.en: Every vacation I stay a few days at my relatives' house in the city.

explain: '도시'보다 조금 예스럽고, 시골이나 농촌과 대비해서 '큰 마을'이라는 느낌으로 말할 때 많이 써요. 반대말은 '시골'이에요. 요즘 대화에서는 그냥 '도시'라고 하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: It sounds a little more old-fashioned than '도시' and is often used in contrast with the countryside. Its opposite is '시골'. In everyday conversation people more often just say '도시'.

examples.en: That neighborhood is a well-known wealthy area in Seoul.

examples.ko: 부촌에 사는 사람들은 집이 정말 커요.
examples.en: The people living in the wealthy area have really big houses.
This area has been known as a wealthy neighborhood for a long time.
It's near a wealthy area, so housing prices are very high.

examples.ko: 부촌과 달리 이쪽 동네는 조용하고 소박해요.
examples.en: Unlike the wealthy area, this neighborhood is quiet and modest.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 부촌 풍경이 현실과 너무 달라요.
examples.en: The wealthy neighborhood in the drama looks too different from reality.

explain: 부동산이나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이고, 일상에서는 '부자 동네'라고도 해요. 반대로 가난한 동네는 '빈촌'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It often appears in real estate and news, and in daily talk people also say '부자 동네' (rich neighborhood). A poor neighborhood is called a '빈촌'.

examples.en: There is a parking lot on the north side of the building.
Please come in through the north entrance.

examples.ko: 산의 북측 사면은 눈이 늦게 녹아요.
examples.en: The snow melts late on the north slope of the mountain.
If you walk to the north side of the lake, there is an observatory.

examples.ko: 이 방은 북측이라 햇빛이 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: This room faces north, so it doesn't get much sunlight.
The northern delegation arrived at the meeting venue first.

explain: '북쪽'은 방향이고, '북측'은 어떤 건물이나 장소의 북쪽 편을 조금 딱딱하게 말하는 거예요. 반대는 '남측'이에요. 뉴스에서는 '북측'이 남북 회담에서 북한 쪽을 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: '북쪽' is a direction, while '북측' is a slightly formal way to say the north side of a building or place. Its opposite is '남측'. In the news, '북측' can also refer to the North Korean side in inter-Korean talks.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 마을에서 외떨어져 있어서 조용해요.
examples.en: Our house is isolated from the village, so it's quiet.

examples.ko: 외떨어진 섬에는 배로만 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only reach the remote island by boat.
The farther you are from the city, the cheaper the housing tends to be.

examples.ko: 회사가 시내에서 너무 외떨어져서 출퇴근이 힘들어요.
examples.en: The company is so far from downtown that commuting is hard.
Buses now run even to the village that used to be isolated.

examples.ko: 학교가 외떨어지다 보니 학생이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Since the school is so remote, there aren't many students.

explain: 다른 곳과 멀리 떨어져 있다는 느낌으로, 대부분 '외떨어진 마을', '외떨어진 곳'처럼 장소를 꾸며 줘요. 사람이 혼자 고립된 상황은 '외톨이가 되다'나 '고립되다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of being far from other places, and is mostly used to describe places, as in '외떨어진 마을' or '외떨어진 곳'. For a person left alone, '외톨이가 되다' or '고립되다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: In the old days, villagers gathered around the well.
My grandmother did the laundry by the well.
There was a big persimmon tree next to the well.
The area around a well is a dangerous place for children.

examples.ko: 영화 속 우물가 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The scene by the well in the movie was impressive.
I went to the well to fetch water.

explain: 우물 둘레를 말하는데, 옛 마을의 모습을 떠올리게 하는 말이에요. 요즘 생활보다는 옛이야기나 드라마에서 많이 들려요. '물가', '강가'처럼 '-가'가 붙어서 그 곁이라는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: It means the area around a well, and it brings to mind scenes of old villages. You hear it more in old tales and dramas than in modern life. Like '물가' and '강가', the '-가' adds the sense of 'beside' something.

examples.en: Steel is made at a steel mill.
My father works at a steel mill on the southern coast.
The area near the steel mill is bright with lights even at night.
On a tour of the steel mill, I saw a blast furnace.
Thousands of people work at a large steel mill.

examples.ko: 제철소가 생긴 뒤로 이 도시가 커졌어요.
examples.en: This city grew after the steel mill was built.

explain: '제철'은 철을 만드는 일이고, 뒤에 '소'가 붙어 그 일을 하는 곳이 돼요. '제철 과일'의 '제철'은 그 계절에 한창인 때라서 전혀 다른 말이에요. 구리나 아연 같은 금속을 만드는 곳은 '제련소'라고 해요.
explain_en: '제철' is the making of iron, and '소' makes it the place. The '제철' in '제철 과일' is the season when something is at its best, a completely different word. A place that refines metals like copper or zinc is a '제련소'.

examples.en: The lower floors of this building have a parking lot.
If you go down to the lower level, you will find the subway station.

examples.ko: 하층에서 나는 공사 소리가 위층까지 올라와요.
examples.en: Construction noise from the lower floor travels up to the upper floors.

examples.ko: 하층 주민들은 홍수가 나면 피해가 커요.
examples.en: Residents of the lower floors suffer more when a flood hits.

examples.ko: 사회의 하층에서 일하는 사람들의 이야기를 다룬 책이에요.
examples.en: It is a book about people working in the lower layers of society.
We turned off the lights in order, starting from the lower floor.

explain: 건물의 층과 사회 계층 두 가지에 쓰는 글 투의 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 건물이면 '아래층'을 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '상층'이에요. 사람을 하층이라고 부르면 낮추는 느낌이 있어서 조심해요.
explain_en: It covers both building levels and social classes, in a written style. In daily talk '아래층' is more common for buildings. The opposite is '상층'. Calling people '하층' sounds belittling, so be careful.
